Nov 27 — Operation: Black Friday Blitz

Bud’s Lunch

Black Friday in the lab, and Brain is still celebrating Thanksgiving: in full Bears gear, he’s munching the Nike Zoom Hyperflight Pink card, with the B&W Pi6 and Nike Foamposite Pro Gym Red cards spread on the table. Behind him the chalkboard has the final — “BEARS 39, LIONS 35 — SIX IN A ROW!” — with a corner note staking a claim: “JOEY — THE FOAMPOSITES ARE MINE”. Operation: Black Friday Blitz is officially underway.

THE FEATURE

The Lights Flip On, and the City Follows

Stevie Wonder turns fifty years of Songs into one night at the United Center, while the holiday switch flips across the whole city — and the rooms in Crystal Lake and Woodstock light up too.

The weekend the whole city lights up, the rooms fill with the biggest names of the season and the holiday switch flips everywhere at once. Stevie Wonder brings his Songs in the Key of Life 50th Anniversary Tour to the United Center on Saturday night, and the week keeps the pace: John Summit's CTRL ESCAPE Arena Tour takes the same room Tuesday and Wednesday, Brent Faiyaz returns to American stages after three years on Monday the 30th, and the Aragon Ballroom runs a three-night gauntlet of Beartooth on Friday, Trivium on Saturday, and Underoath's Define the Great Line 20th Anniversary Tour on Tuesday. Fetty Wap's Nostalgia Tour hits The Salt Shed Friday, George Lopez takes the Chicago Theatre Saturday, Little Big Town opened the week there Thursday, and the Bears host the Saints at Soldier Field Sunday at noon. Friday is also the night the city turns on its holiday lights — Christkindlmarket, the Millennium Park tree lighting, ZooLights, and the McCormick Tribune Ice Rink all open, with the Magnificent Mile Lights Festival following on Saturday.

Closer to home, the season starts on local stages. The Santa Switch, Raue Center's holiday jukebox musical, opens Friday night in Crystal Lake and runs through December 6, with a special Festival of Lights performance on Friday the 27th. Annie plays its final weekend at the Woodstock Opera House, November 27 through 29, and the McHenry Downtown Holiday Walk brings the Cocoa Crawl, sleigh rides, Santa, and a Toys for Tots parade this weekend. The MCC Concert Band closes out Sunday afternoon at Woodstock High School. Chicago gets the headliners this week — but the county gets the first taste of Christmas.

Bud’s Field Notes

3 NOTES · NOV 27

The trail shoe is the collab shoe now.

WTAPS x HOKA Speedgoat TS drops today at $175, and the SOMEWHERE x ASICS GEL-Stratus MC lands tomorrow at $110 — both carded in Limited Collabs at retail. Technical trail silhouettes, not retro runners, are the fashion collab vehicle this week. The Speedgoat is a real trail shoe with a WTAPS badge; buy the drop, never the resale ask.

Nike’s own site is beating resale on its own retros.

The BFRIDAY code carded in Fresh Finds — Kobe Air Force 1 at $71.98 (was $125), Jordan Skyline at $61, Revolution 7 at $34 (was $70) — has Nike direct undercutting the resale market on its own shoes this week. The code ends Nov 29. The mall isn’t the cheapest lane right now; Nike is.

The deepest Black Friday cuts are on the gear that never discounts.

Garmin Instinct 3 Solar, $449.99 → $289.99. Citizen Promaster Dive, $450 → $315. Both carded in Fresh Finds. The watches that sit at full price all year are where the real 30%+ lives — the stuff that’s always on sale just gets another sticker.

UFC Fight Night 295: Adesanya vs. Shara Magomedov

ANB ARENA · RIYADH, SAUDI ARABIA
MAIN EVENTMAIN 12PM CT
Main event · Middleweight · 5 rounds
Israel Adesanya vs. Shara Magomedov

Israel Adesanya · 24-6 · former two-time MW champ

Age37
Height6'4"
Reach80"
StanceSwitch
Note4-fight skid, winless since 2023

Shara Magomedov · 17-1 · #15 MW

Age32
Height6'2"
Reach73"
StanceOrthodox
Note6-1 UFC · 12 KO · blind in one eye

Adesanya: former two-time middleweight champion fighting to keep his elite era alive — a 7-inch reach edge (80" vs 73") is his whole game plan. Magomedov: #15 MW, a one-eyed pressure finisher who has to cross that reach to win.

ODDS AS OF NOV 27, 2026 — LINES MOVEAdesanya −166 / Magomedov +140 · DraftKings
Co-main · Welterweight · 5 rounds
#1 Ian Machado Garry vs. #12 Yaroslav Amosov

Garry (17-2, 29, 6'3", 74" reach, orthodox): lands 4.29 sig strikes/min, absorbs just 2.59, defends 71% of takedowns. His only losses are five-round decisions to Shavkat Rakhmonov and, this August, to Islam Makhachev in a title fight. Around those he beat Carlos Prates and Belal Muhammad. Amosov (30-1, 33, 6'0", 75" reach, orthodox): the most extreme wrestling weapon on the card — 11.11 takedowns per 15 min, 3.17 submission attempts per 15. Both UFC wins ended by submission in R2 or earlier (anaconda choke on Neil Magny, arm-triangle on Joel Alvarez). 13 of his 30 wins are submissions. His only loss: Jason Jackson, Nov 2023, cost him the Bellator title. The read: Garry's range, output and takedown defense answer the one question Amosov asks — but Amosov only needs one completed takedown chain, and the longer the fight runs, the more attempts he gets. Winner's next step: an Amosov win likely means a title shot vs Makhachev in 2027; a Garry win puts him back in the title queue after the Makhachev loss.

ODDS AS OF NOV 27, 2026 — LINES MOVEGarry −170 / Amosov +142 · DraftKings
Bud’s take — Adesanya vs. Magomedov: A range war — Adesanya's 7-inch reach edge and switch-step calf kick against Shara's busier, weirder pressure. Adesanya's path: control range with the switch step and calf kick, make Shara reset after the first kick, counter on the way back in, and let five rounds do the work. Championship-rounds experience is his clearest edge. This fight is a referendum on his reflexes and timing, not his résumé — winless since 2023, on a 4-fight skid, now out of a brand-new camp. Shara's path: cross the gap, accept the return, throw the next one anyway. He lands 5.55 sig strikes/min at 62% accuracy (Adesanya: 4.03 at 48%) and his equalizer is unorthodoxy — the double spinning backfist that KO'd Armen Petrosyan, creative angles, relentless pressure. His blueprint loss is the Michael Page fight (Feb 2025) — a long, awkward striker frustrated him over three rounds. Adesanya's job is the Page script with better tools. The one thing to watch: whether Adesanya's timing is still sharp after the skid — and whether Shara's deep-water cardio holds past round 3, untested over five rounds. Neither man has a takedown game (0.00–0.05 TD avg) — this stays on the feet. Shara is blind in one eye, which is why most US commissions won't license him and why this fight lives in Riyadh. Stakes: Adesanya — a loss makes it five straight and the comeback story dies; a win re-opens the middleweight top 5. Shara — a win over a former two-time champ in his first main event puts him in the title conversation at 32.

New camp: Adesanya fights out of a new camp — Unity MMA, not City Kickboxing — after a split he called ‘worse than a breakup,’ citing ‘disrespect’ and ‘manipulation’ after 16 years with Eugene Bareman. His corner team now: Andrei Paulet (ex-CKB wrestling coach) and Tristam ‘Twist’ Apikotoa.
